arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Kansas advocate John Draper presented three issues for the Court.
United States advocate Feldman agreed with Colorado on the river master issue.
Colorado advocate Robbins disputed the similarity of other river compacts.
Justices questioned the logic of using a ten-year model for dry years.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: Kansas argues the current water measurement method is flawed. The state wants a river master to manage the dispute. Colorado opposes appointing a new official. It argues the existing legal framework handles the issue well.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: Kansas wants the Court to appoint a river master to manage the water dispute.
Colorado wants the Court to reject the appointment of a river master.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: Kansas argues the current ten-year model unfairly penalizes dry years.
Colorado argues the existing decree and model adequately conserve subsurface reservoirs.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: The outcome determines how states calculate water credits during dry years. It also decides whether a new official manages interstate water disputes. This affects future resource allocation between neighboring states.
